Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 8, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿They ask you about the spoils of war. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger. So fear Allah, set right what is between you, and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers.﴾

Tafsir of Surat al-Anfal

The Shaykh, the Imam, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Surat al-Anfal is Medinan except for seven verses, namely from His saying ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you﴾ to the end of the seven verses, for they were revealed in Mecca. Most of the surah concerns the Battle of Badr.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾. Asking (su'al) is of two kinds: a question seeking information (su'al istikhbar) and a question seeking a request (su'al talab). His saying ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾ is a question seeking information, for they asked him about the ruling on the spoils.

Ibn Mas'ud and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas recited: "They ask you for the spoils" (yas'alunaka al-anfal), and this is a question seeking a request. Mus'ab ibn Sa'd narrated from his father, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, that he said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah for a sword on the day of Badr, and I said: 'Grant it to me, O Messenger of Allah.' So the verse ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾ was revealed."

Al-anfal means the spoils of war (al-ghana'im). Linguistically, nafl means increase, and Labid ibn Rabi'a al-Amiri said in verse:

(Indeed, the piety of our Lord is the best increase... and with the permission of Allah is delay and haste.)

From this comes voluntary prayer (salat al-nafila), because it is an increase over the obligatory prayer. The spoils were named anfal because they are an additional honour from Allah, exalted is He, specifically for this Ummah.

The occasion of revelation of the verse is what is narrated: that the Companions of the Prophet divided on the day of Badr into two groups: a group that fought and took captives, and a group that guarded the Messenger of Allah. Then they disputed. The fighting group said: "The spoils are ours; we fought and took captives." The others said: "We were a support for you, and we guarded the Messenger of Allah, so the spoils are between us." So the verse ﴿They ask you about the spoils﴾ was revealed.

In another narration: "The Prophet said on that day: Whoever kills a slain enemy, for him is such and such, and whoever takes a captive, for him is such and such." So the young men hastened, fought and took captives, while the elders remained with the Messenger, may peace be upon him, guarding him. Then they disputed over the spoils. The young men said: "The spoils are ours, because we fought." The elders said: "We were guarding the Messenger of Allah, and we were a support for you." The one who spoke among the young men was Abu al-Yusr, and the one who spoke among the elders was Sa'd ibn Mu'adh. So the verse was revealed, and the Prophet divided the spoils among all of them.

As for His saying ﴿Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾, the scholars differed concerning it. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: the verse is abrogated (mansukha) by the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of booty, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger﴾. This verse returned the matter from the whole to the fifth, so it was abrogating (nasikha) of the first.

It was also said: the verse is not abrogated, and the meaning of His saying ﴿Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾ is that their ruling belongs to Allah and the Messenger, so it agrees with that verse.

As for ﴿So fear Allah and set right what is between you﴾, Tha'lab said: it means set right the state that is between you. Its meaning is reconciliation by abandoning dispute and committing the matter of the spoils to Allah and the Messenger. ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 8, verse 2:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the believers are those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned﴾. Ibn Abi Najih said: That is, they were frightened and apprehensive. The poet said:

(By your life, I do not know, though I am greatly fearful... on which of us death will come first)

﴿And when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith﴾: that is, in certainty and affirmation. This is because whenever a verse was revealed and they believed in it, their faith and affirmation increased. This is evidence for the Ahl al-Sunnah (the People of the Sunnah) that faith increases and decreases. ﴿And upon their Lord they rely﴾. Tawakkul (reliance) is depending upon Allah and placing trust in Him.

ـ(The ones who establish the prayer and spend out of what We have provided for them) ﴿Those who establish the prayer and spend out of what We have provided for them﴾. Establishing the prayer means performing it at its appointed times, with its conditions and pillars.

Verse 4 of Surah al-Anfal (8):

﴿Those are the true believers.﴾ Muqatil said: that is, faith free of any doubt. It was also said: they are cleared of disbelief and hypocrisy.

In this verse there is evidence for the Ahl al-Sunnah (the People of the Sunnah) that it is not permissible for anyone to describe himself as a true believer (mu'min haqqan), because God, exalted is He, only ascribes this to specific people with specific characteristics, and not everyone can be certain in himself that those characteristics are present.

﴿For them there are ranks with their Lord, and forgiveness and a generous provision.﴾ Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: the ranks are seventy degrees, and between each two degrees is the distance a galloping horse covers in seventy years. ﴿Generous provision﴾ means complete, with no deficiency in it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 8, verses 5–6:

The words of His, exalted is He: ﴿As your Lord brought you forth from your house in truth﴾. Most scholars hold that this refers to His bringing him forth from Madinah to Badr for fighting against the polytheists. It was also said that it refers to his bringing forth from Makkah to Madinah.

They differed over what the comparative particle (kaf al-tashbih) in His words ﴿As He brought you forth﴾ refers back to. Al-Mubarrad said: its implied sense is: "The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger, even though they dislike it, just as your Lord brought you forth from your house even though they disliked it." The view of al-Farra' is close to this, and so is the view of al-Zajjaj; for both of them said: its implied sense is: "Proceed according to the command of Allah concerning the spoils, even though they dislike it, just as you proceeded according to the command of Allah when He brought you forth from your house, even though they disliked it."

It was also said that it refers back to His words, exalted is He: ﴿So fear Allah﴾, and its implied sense is: "Just as your Lord brought you forth from your house in truth, so follow His command: fear Allah and set right what is between you." It was also said that it refers back to His words, exalted is He: ﴿For them are ranks with their Lord﴾, and its implied sense is: "The promise of ranks is true, just as your Lord brought you forth from your house in truth; so He fulfilled the promise of victory and triumph." Abu 'Ubaydah said: "ma" here has the meaning of "alladhi" (that which), i.e., "like that which your Lord brought you forth with."

﴿And indeed, a party of the believers were averse,  ﴾ ﴿arguing with you concerning the truth after it had become clear﴾. This is because the companions of the Messenger of Allah disliked his going out to Badr, and argued about it, saying: "We will not go out, for we have not prepared for fighting, and we do not have the equipment of war with us."

His words ﴿after it had become clear﴾ mean: after its truthfulness had become clear to them regarding what he had promised them time and again, so they affirmed his promise.

﴿As though they were being driven to death while they were looking on﴾. There is an inversion (taqdim and ta'khir) in this, and its implied sense is: "And indeed, a party of the believers were averse to it, as though they were being driven to death while they were looking on, arguing with you concerning the truth after it had become clear."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 8, verse 7:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours﴾. The cause of this: it is related that Abu Sufyan came with a caravan from the direction of al-Sham, in which were the wealth of Quraysh. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions in Madinah, so they set out in pursuit of the caravan. Abu Sufyan sent a man to Makkah to call them to arms (yastanfiruhum) and to seek their aid (yastaghithu bihim). So Abu Jahl and the leaders of the polytheists came out, seven hundred and fifty men. The Muslims on that day were three hundred and thirteen men, and they had little weaponry; they had only two horses, one belonging to al-Miqdad ibn 'Amr and the other to Abu Marthad al-Ghanawi. With them were six coats of mail, and most of them were on foot, while some were on camels. Allah, may He be exalted, promised them one of the two groups: either the caravan (aw) or the troop (al-nafir). Abu Sufyan was the owner of the caravan, and Abu Jahl was the owner of the troop. Then the two hosts met and came to fighting, while the caravan took the coastal road and got away. The Muslims wished to seize the caravan and gain the wealth without fighting. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿and you wished that the unarmed one would be yours﴾. And al-shawka is the weapons.

﴿And Allah intends to establish the truth by His words﴾, that is: to make the truth manifest and to exalt His word. ﴿And to cut off the last of the disbelievers﴾, that is: the root of the disbelievers.
﴿That He might establish the truth and nullify falsehood﴾, i.e., He establishes the truth and negates falsehood, ﴿even though the criminals disliked it﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 8, verse 9:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿When you sought help from your Lord﴾. Al-istighathah (seeking relief, calling for help) means seeking ghawth (relief). ﴿So He answered you: "I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another."﴾ The cause of this is what has been related: that when the two hosts met at Badr, the Prophet (ﷺ) faced the qiblah, raised his hands, and said: "O Allah, fulfil for me what You promised me. O Allah, if this band perishes, You will not be worshipped on the earth." He raised his voice with it, and Abu Bakr said to him: "Lower your voice, O Messenger of Allah; for Allah will surely fulfil for you what He has promised you." Then the verse was revealed, and He answered his supplication and aided them with the angels. It has been related: "Jibril descended with five hundred, and Mika'il with five hundred, and upon their heads were white turbans whose ends hung down between their shoulders, and they were in the form of men, upon piebald horses." This is the meaning of His words: ﴿So He answered you: "I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another."﴾ It is said: radifahu and ardafahu, meaning (atba'ahu), he followed him. The poet said:

(When al-Jawza' followed al-Thurayya, I suspected the family of Fatimah of suspicions.)

So the meaning of His words ﴿murdifin﴾ is: following one another, one after another. This is the meaning of the second recitation with a fathah on the dal. Some distinguished between the two and said: ﴿murdifin﴾ means reinforcing one another. As for the one who reads with a fathah on the dal, its meaning is: reinforced from before Allah.

The Exalted's words: ﴿And Allah made it not but as good news﴾, meaning: as glad tidings, ﴿and that your hearts might be assured thereby﴾, meaning: that your hearts might be settled thereby. ﴿And victory is not but from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, All-Wise﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 8, verse 11:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When He covered you with drowsiness as a security from Him﴾. It is also recited as "إِذْ يغشاكم النعاس" (idh yaghshākumu al-nu'ās, "when drowsiness overtook you"). Ibn Muhayṣin recited "أَمَنَة" (amanah) with a sukun on the mim, which is an irregular reading (shādhdh).

The story behind this is that on the day of Badr the disbelievers descended at the water, while the Muslims descended at a place without water. Some of them were in a state of major impurity (janabah) and some in a state of minor impurity (ḥadath), and they found no water with which to purify themselves. They were on sand in which their feet sank. Satan whispered to them: "You claim that you are upon the truth and they are upon falsehood, yet they are at the water while you are not. If you were upon the truth, you would be at the water, and you would not remain in a state of impurity." A severe fear fell upon them, so God, may He be exalted, cast drowsiness upon them until they were secure. He brought forth a cloud which rained upon them until the valley flowed, and they purified themselves and performed ghusl, and the sand was packed down until feet could stand firm upon it. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿When He covered you with drowsiness as a security﴾.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "Drowsiness in battle is from God, and drowsiness in prayer is from Satan."

﴿And He sends down upon you water from the sky to purify you thereby﴾, which is what we have mentioned, ﴿and to remove from you the defilement of Satan﴾, i.e., the whispering of Satan, ﴿and to strengthen your hearts﴾, i.e., to make your hearts firm and steadfast by removing fear, ﴿and to make firm the feet thereby﴾, meaning: upon the sand when it was packed down by the rain.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 8, verse 12:

﴿When your Lord inspired the angels: "I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed."﴾ That is: with victory and triumph. ﴿I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, so strike above the necks.﴾ That is: upon the necks. It was also said: "fawq" here is extra (ṣila), and its meaning is: strike the necks. It was also said: it remains in its place, and its meaning is: strike on the crown of the head (al-yāfūkh).

﴿And strike from them every fingertip.﴾ It was said: al-bunān is the joints of the extremities; it was also said: the fingers. It is as if it were an expression for the hands and feet.

Ibn al-Anbārī said: The angels did not know how human beings are killed, so God taught them.

It was also said: the angels did not fight except at the Battle of Badr.

And from Ibn Mas'ūd, may Allah be pleased with him: when he wanted to cut off the head of Abū Jahl, who had mounted him to kill him, Abū Jahl said to him: "We used to hear the sound but not see a person, and see the blows but not see the one who strikes. Who are they?" He said: "They are the angels." Abū Jahl said: "Those have overcome us, not you."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 8, verses 13–14:

﴿That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger.﴾ That is: they contended against Allah and His Messenger.

﴿And whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, indeed Allah is severe in punishment. That, so taste it; and for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire.﴾ He said that (taste it) as an intensification in punishment and retribution. The Arabs say to an enemy when a calamity befalls him: "Dhuq" (taste). Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Taste it, indeed you were the mighty, the noble.﴾

It is narrated that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, when he passed by Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, who was lying slain on the day of Uhud, said to him: "Dhuq, ya 'uqq," meaning: "Taste it, you disobedient one."

In the story: when the Muslims finished fighting at Badr and the disbelievers were routed, they intended to pursue the caravan (al-'Ir) and to follow them. Al-'Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib was in the custody and captivity of the Muslims. He said to them: "There is no way for you to that; for Allah the Exalted has promised you one of the two groups, and you have won over the army, so the caravan is not for you." So they fell silent.

﴿That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger.﴾ That is: they contended against Allah and His Messenger.

﴿And whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, indeed Allah is severe in punishment.
